scope: independent host-side oracle validation only; no device access, no ssh/scp, no submit, no RTL simulation, no program/flash

method.neg: decoded as EW_OP_TYPE=MUL with B weight -1.0
method.fdiv: exact rational quotient rounded to binary16 nearest-even; validated against the real captured finite sweep
method.int: source integer_expected saturation semantics; INT32 MUL applies the source-captured signed-INT16 operand rule
method.inputs: decoded from a.bin/b.bin, not from expected.bin; layout decoded/repacked with the source C1WC2 rule

fdiv_validation.rule: round-to-nearest, ties-to-even of the exact quotient
fdiv_validation.note: All 32 finite-sweep and 11 finite special-capture lanes match exact-rational nearest-even. Six sweep lanes reject truncation toward zero; eight exact subnormal-range ties (six in the sweep, two in the special capture) confirm ties-to-even. The four README 'RK-specific' quotients are correctly rounded under nearest-even, so that wording is not supported by the capture.

manifest_special_values: tail lane 8 lands in the third 16-byte surface
31000 exceeds INT16 range but must stay 31000 in INT32 output

structural_issues.issue: documentation claim is false: manifest/README says lane 7 saturates, but the decoded operands produce 105, which is inside [-128, 127] for INT8
documentation claim is false: manifest/README says lane 7 saturates, but the decoded operands produce 31000, which is inside [-32768, 32767] for INT16
documentation claim is false: manifest/README says lane 0 saturates, but the decoded operands produce -31000, which is inside [-32768, 32767] for INT16

coverage_gaps.gap: no Inf/NaN operands or results in any case
coverage_gaps.detail: finite-only family; NaN canonicalization and the SUB infinity quirk are not exercised.

coverage_gaps.gap: no subnormal inputs or subnormal/underflow results
coverage_gaps.detail: smallest magnitudes are 0.125 (1/8) and 0.5; no lane reaches the 2^-14 normal boundary or 2^-24 subnormal unit.

coverage_gaps.gap: no overflow/Inf result, no signed-zero operand
coverage_gaps.detail: largest result is 8192; only +0 appears (p2 A and padded lanes), no -0 operand for MAX/sign-of-zero policy.

coverage_gaps.gap: physical 8-lane padding lanes are never asserted
coverage_gaps.detail: N=1,7,9,33 cases process 8/16/40 lanes but expected.bin covers only N. A tail lane-shift or padded-lane write bug is invisible; recommended assertion is +0 for non-FDIV padded lanes and +0 for FDIV 0/1 lanes.

coverage_gaps.gap: ADD/SUB never round; MUL/FDIV rounding is sparse
coverage_gaps.detail: all 1132 ADD and 1132 SUB lane results are exactly representable binary16. MUL (incl. NEG) has 98 inexact lanes of 2264; FDIV has 413 inexact of 1132. No round-half tie is constructed on purpose.

coverage_gaps.gap: MAX has no unsigned/encoded-magnitude edge and no NaN tie
coverage_gaps.detail: MAX lanes are positive-vs-positive or negative-vs-positive; the equal pair at p2 lane 28 is the only tie, and no -0/+0 ordering case exists.

coverage_gaps.gap: FDIV rounding evidence is only 32 finite sweep lanes
coverage_gaps.detail: nearest-even and eight subnormal exact ties are confirmed, but only 32 captured lanes exist; no normal-range exact tie, no quotient just above the subnormal/normal boundary, and no flush-to-zero policy test.

coverage_gaps.gap: logical N is metadata, not encoded in regcmd
coverage_gaps.detail: only padded=8*(width+1) is in the command stream; N comes from manifest/expected.bin length. A worker cannot infer N from the device command alone.

coverage_gaps.gap: no saturation/overflow lane exists anywhere in the family
coverage_gaps.detail: the manifest claims three saturating lanes, but all three are inside range: INT8 lane 7 is 100+5=105 in [-128,127], INT16 lane 7 is 30000+1000=31000 in [-32768,32767], INT16 lane 0 is -30000-1000=-31000 in range. INT8/INT16 MUL use small operands; INT32 MUL products are ~5e7, far below 2^31. The saturation policy is therefore entirely untested despite the documentation.

coverage_gaps.gap: no exact saturation boundary or signed-overflow edge
coverage_gaps.detail: no +127/+128/-128/-129, +/-32767/+/-32768, and no INT32 2^31-1/2^31 boundary; no INT32_MIN operand; no double-overflow (e.g. 100+100) lane.

coverage_gaps.gap: INT32 MUL full-width semantics are only rejected, not measured
coverage_gaps.detail: the bundle asserts the signed-INT16 operand model (50000 -> -15536, -50000 -> 15536). A full INT32 operand would produce different results, so a device mismatch is informative candidate behavior, not a bundle bug. No b=0x8000/-32768 lane and no product exactly on 2^31-1 or -2^31 is included.

coverage_gaps.gap: INT8/INT16 MUL reuse one small operand vector
coverage_gaps.detail: both MUL cases submit the same MUL_A_8/MUL_B_8 values (-8,-6,... / 3,-2,...), replacing the source DTYPES vectors. No MUL saturation or signed-product boundary is exercised for INT8 or INT16.

coverage_gaps.gap: INT32 layout 9-channel stream is offline-only in the source
coverage_gaps.detail: the source never claims a device pass for that exact combination; a device mismatch there is an open question.
INT8 asserted 8 of 16 surface bytes, INT8 layout 9 of 16, INT16 layout 18 of 32, INT32 layout 36 of 48. A padding corruption or a surface-stride bug in unused slots is invisible by design.
no INT32 MIN/MINUS, no INT8/INT16 MIN beyond one INT8 case, no INT8 MINUS, no ABS/NEG/FLOOR/CEIL; DIV/FLOOR/CEIL are proven floating-point and correctly BLOCKED.

caveats: All expected.bin files are host oracles, never device outputs; these checks only validate bundle consistency and source fidelity.

model/half.py is an independent binary16 model that also encodes captured RK quirks (NaN 0x7c01, ADD/SUB zero -> +0, SUB infinity rule, MAX signed-zero ordering). It is not an RK silicon specification.

The FP16 input patterns p1/p2 are deterministic preparation-time closed forms, not the source examples' seeded np.random.uniform data; the arithmetic formula is the source donor formula, the operands are not.
INT saturation is candidate behavior: it follows the source's integer_expected clip(), but no bundled lane actually overflows, so the capture cannot establish the device's saturation policy.
INT32 MUL signed-INT16 operand is a source-captured limitation and candidate behavior, not a documented ABI.

The FDIV oracle is exact-rational nearest-even; the real sweep covers 32 lanes and the special capture 11 finite lanes with nonzero divisor, including eight exact subnormal-range ties. Normal-range exact ties and the full rounding space are not covered.
No local RTL, Verilator, FPGA or RK3588 execution was used or is claimed; C++/RTL results would not be device evidence anyway.
No ssh/scp/192.168.192.18 access, no submit, no program or flash.

covered_points.point: INT32 MUL signed-INT16 operand is exercised
covered_points.detail: lanes 0,1,6,7 carry b=50000/-50000; they decode as -15536/+15536 and the oracle products are 15,536,000 / -31,072,000 / 31,072,000 / -15,536,000. All four differ from the full-int32 product. Candidate behavior, not a documented ABI.
the 9-channel layout cases assert the tail lane in the second/third 16-byte surface (INT8 9/16, INT16 18/32, INT32 36/48 asserted bytes).
9 finite FDIV cases compare 1132 lanes, 413 of them inexact; the exact-rational nearest-even oracle also reproduces all 32 captured finite-sweep lanes and the 11 finite lanes of the special capture.

covered_points.point: exact cancellation and signed zero result
covered_points.detail: ADD p2 has +0 results at lanes 2/11; SUB p2 n33 has a run of five exact cancellations at lanes 28..32; NEG p2 produces -0.0 (0x8000) at lanes 5/16/27.
A=B=0.5; the oracle and bundle return 0x3800. No signed-zero or NaN MAX ordering is covered.
